 1. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR (AP)

The Court made the following:
COMMON ORDER:
Criminal Petition Nos.720, 870, 875, 903 and 904 of 2020 under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 19731 have been filed by the Petitioners/Accused Nos.,26, 31, 32, 28 and 36 respectively,
seeking to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.23 of 2020 on the file of Dhone Town Urban Police Station, Kurnool District, which was registered for the offence punishable under Sections 328, 420 and 120B read with 34 of Indian Penal Code, 18602 and Section 34(a) of A.P.Excise Act3. 1 for short 'Cr.P.C' for short 'IPC' for short 'the Act'
2.

The facts mentioned in the complaint, in brief, are as follows:
a. On 28.01.2020 at 5.00 p.m., at the open empty place behind Perantalamma temple at a distance of 1.k., from NH 44 road running between Kambalapadu village and Dhone Town, Accused Nos.4, 5 and 7 were found in possession of 70 liters of illicit spirit contained in two plastic cans and they were also found in possession of one white colour plastic bag containing 3,000 I.B whisky bottle caps and two yellow colour bags containing 1500 Mc.Dowell whisky bottle caps and 1500 other caps and the said contraband was seized from them under the cover of panchanama. b.

It is further alleged that Accused Nos.1 to 36 in furtherance of criminal conspiracy,
prepared an underground bunk in the house of Accused No.6 and made spurious liquor by adding spirit and transported them illegally and sold the same without having valid license from the Government.
c. Accused Nos.2, 23 and 26 to 36 formed a syndicate group with the influence of high handed persons to supply spurious liquor to all the wine shops in Dhone Town and its surrounding villages.
As such, a case in Crime No.23 of 2020 has been registered against Accused Nos.1 to 36 for the offence under Sections 328, 420 and 120B read with 34 of IPC and Section 34(a) of the Act.
The allegations made against the Petitioners are vague in nature and do not constitute any offence and they were made with a malafide intention. b.
The Petitioners have not committed the alleged offence and Respondent No.2 under the pressure from political parties is trying to initiate false case against the Petitioners.

Marri Sriramulu, vs State Of Rep on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44699986/
2 c.

sentences.text: The FIR in the present case was registered on 28.01.2020 and the offence occurred on 29.01.2020 at about 5.00 p.m. d.
Except the confessional statements made by the co-accused, which are inadmissible, there is no legally admissible evidence against the Petitioners.
The confessional statement of Accused No.2 clearly establishes that he was not aware of running of liquor business as alleged and it was only told to him by one Ayyappa and Balaji Sreenu.
Accused No.2 is not aware of the role of the Petitioners in the business.
There is no direct evidence for the involvement of the Petitioners in the alleged crime.
e. There is no evidence to show the commission of alleged offence by the Petitioners.
Therefore, continuation of proceedings against the Petitioners is an abuse of process of laws.

Arguments Advanced at the Bar 4. Heard Sri C.B.Siddarth, learned counsel for the Petitioner/Accused No.26, Sri I.Venkata Prasad,
learned counsel for Petitioner/Accused Nos.28, 31 and 36.
Sri Nagaraju Naguru, learned counsel for Petitioner/Accused No.32 and Ms.D.Prasanna Lakshmi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the State.
5. Learned Counsel for the Petitioners would submit that based on the confession only, the present case has been registered.

It is further submitted that Petitioner/Accused No.26 filed nomination in the elections, as such, due to political rivalry, the Petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present case and nothing is found in the searches conducted in the houses at Hyderabad and Kurnool.

It is also submitted that there no specific overt acts attributed against the Petitioners,
hence, continuation of proceedings against the Petitioners is an abuse of process of law.
6.
Per contra, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, would submit that, there are clear allegations against the Petitioners which would attract the alleged offences.
Because of stay of investigation against one of the Accused, investigation in the present case could not be proceeded.
The truth of the allegations will be proved after completion of investigation only.

When there are disputed facts to be revealed during enquiry, this Court cannot exercise its jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C.,
at this stage.
Therefore, Court cannot quash the proceedings against the Petitioners.
Hence, pray for dismissal of the petition.
Point for Determination 7.

Having heard the submissions of the learned counsel representing both the parties, now the point that would emerge for determination is:
Whether there are any justifiable grounds for quashment of proceedings against the Petitioners/ Accused Nos.26, 31, 32, 28 and 36 in Crime No.23 of 2020 on the file of Dhone Town Urban Police Station, Kurnool District?
Determination by the Court Marri Sriramulu, vs State Of Rep on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44699986/
3 8.

sentences.text: A bare perusal of Section 482 makes it clear that the Code envisages that inherent powers of the High Court are not limited or affected so as to make orders as may be necessary; (i) to give effect to any order under the Code or, (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or, otherwise (iii) to secure ends of justice.
A court while sitting in Section 482 jurisdiction is not functioning as a court of appeal or a court of revision.

It must exercise its powers to do real and substantial justice,
depending on the facts and circumstances of the case.

These powers must be invoked for compelling reasons of abuse of process of law or glaring injustice, which are against sound principles of criminal jurisprudence.
9.

As seen from the material available on record, Accused No.2 stated that the Petitioners herein along with other Accused formed a Syndicate and used to sell spurious liquor and transporting the bottles illegally and thereby cheated the public and the Government the spurious liquor, without having any valid license from the Government and their activities gone through the criminal conspiracy and 70 liters of spurious spirit, 3000 IB Whisky caps, 1500 caps of IB whisky bottles and 1500 empty caps of others and 300 MC whisky quarter bottles were seized under the cover of panchanama from the possession of Accused Nos.1, 4 to 8 and 25 and the remaining accused i.e.,
Accused Nos.2, 3 and 9 to 36 also involved in this case.
10.
Though the case was registered based on the confessional statement of Accused No.2, it is difficult at this stage to accept or deny the contention of Accused No.2.
It is for the investigating agency to find out whether the Petitioners herein are responsible for transportation or sale of such liquor without having valid licence.

To find out the truth in the allegations made in the remand report, based on the confessional statement of co-accused, the investigating agency has to make every attempt to find unearth the happening, particularly the complicity of the Petitioners.

In such a case, the Court must scrutinize the material on record and if the Court concludes that the material collected so far prima facie establishes the involvement of the Petitioners in the crime, the Court can refuse to exercise such discretion under Section 482.
The contention of the Petitioners that they were implicated based on the confession of the co-accused, is not a ground to quash the proceedings against them 11.

To quash the proceeding against the Petitioners, it is imperative on the part of the Court to satisfy itself that there is no prima facie material against the Petitioners to establish the criminal accusation.
Further, in the present case, seizure of account books pertaining to syndicate business has also been done.

According to the Public Prosecutor, in view of the stay of proceedings granted in respect of Petitioner/Accused No.26, the investigation is stalled against the other Accused also and it is at nascent stage and such, there was no time for collection of further evidence.

Hence, taking into consideration of gravity of the offence, and the quantity of illicit liquor seized, it is difficult for the Court to exercise the discretion that is vested under Section 482 Cr.P.C, at this stage.

Therefore,
this Court concludes that the allegations made against the Petitioners, in this case, are sufficient enough for the investigation to be taken up and thereby, the proceedings against the Petitioners are not advisable to be quashed and hence, the petitions deserve dismissal 12.
In the result, the Criminal Petitions are dismissed.

However, the Petitioners are at liberty to file fresh petition to question the charge sheet which will be filed after completion of investigation, if so Marri Sriramulu, vs State Of Rep on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44699986/
4 advised.
